content.text:
If you mean the **actual Japanese dwarf flying squirrel** (*Pteromys momonga*), you probably **can’t buy one legally or ethically in the U.S.** It’s a wild squirrel species endemic to Japan, found in places like Honshu and Kyushu, not a normal captive-bred pet species. ([animaldiversity.org](https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Pteromys_momonga/))

Japan’s wildlife rules generally protect wild mammals and birds; capture/hunting of protected non-game species is prohibited unless special permission is granted, and sale/transfer restrictions apply to endangered/designated species. ([env.go.jp](https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/biodiv/wp.html)) Even if you saw online listings, I’d treat them as likely **scams, misidentified animals, or illegally sourced wildlife**.

**Better options:**
- If you want a similar pet, look into **captive-bred Southern flying squirrels** or **sugar gliders**—but check your **state and city laws first**, because exotic pet rules vary widely.
- If you just want to see one, look for **Japanese zoos/wildlife centers** or ethical wildlife tours in Japan rather than trying to buy one.

If you tell me your **state**, I can help check what small gliding mammals are legal near you.
